display.purpose: Monospaced readout for the score and the stopwatch. Largest type in the product; nothing competes with it.

title.purpose: Titles of the three live panels and the tactical control panels.

body.purpose: Explanatory text, feed player names, chat bubbles. Lines under ~75 characters.

label.purpose: Uppercase 11px labels, card titles and KPI captions. Always uppercase.

micro.purpose: Non-numeric micro chrome only (crests, badges). Never a value.

data.purpose: The five headline numbers of the Estadísticas strip.

data-small.purpose: Counters, minutes, per-quarter rows and feed stamps.

icon.purpose: Single-character glyphs inside action tiles, score buttons and the Coach IA button. Never data.

shadows.name: panel-lift
shadows.purpose: Resting shadow of every glass panel. Stat cards carry the same glass and blur but no shadow, so they sit one level flatter than a panel.

shadows.name: control-lift
shadows.purpose: Primary buttons and other raised commit controls.

shadows.name: active-tab
shadows.purpose: Selected top tab and selected player chip: the shadow tightens as the element becomes a solid blue plate.

shadows.name: chip-press
shadows.purpose: Selected category chip, zone button and selected schema chip.

shadows.name: input-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus ring of glass inputs. A ring, never a glow.

shadows.name: score-pop
shadows.purpose: The score animation uses transform scale 1 → 1.22 → 1 over 400ms with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); no shadow is involved.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Default transition for every control: hover, focus, active and selection changes.

motion.name: ease-panel
motion.purpose: Slower transitions for glass surfaces and input fields.

motion.name: ease-score
motion.purpose: The score pop. The one expressive easing in the system; everything else is mechanical.

motion.name: ease-slide
motion.purpose: The Coach IA side panel entering from the right, and the tactical board fade-in.

motion.name: ease-bar
motion.purpose: Width transitions of the statistics progress bars.

motion.name: feed-enter
motion.purpose: New feed rows fade in and rise 8px into place.

motion.name: live-pulse
motion.purpose: The 8px live dot on the Estadísticas badge and the Coach IA panel header: opacity 1 → 0.4 → 1. Only rendered while a match is running.

motion.name: typing-pulse
motion.purpose: The three-dot typing indicator of the Coach IA panel.

rules.zero-green: There is no green in the chrome — no teal, emerald, purple, or indigo anywhere in the shell, panels, tabs, buttons, chips, or charts. The only green permitted is the literal hockey green card.
rules.blue-means-live: Electric blue is a state, not a brand. Before a match starts every live signal stays grey: the Partido tab is dimmed and dotted, the stage label reads Sin Iniciar, and the Estadísticas badge stays off.
rules.no-vertical-scroll: The live view must fit in 100vh with no page-level vertical scroll; overflow is delegated to the action pad, the player grid and the feed.
rules.touch-targets: Minimum 44px of touch height everywhere (56px+ recommended); action tiles are 92px.
rules.mono-data: Every number the user reads as data is set in JetBrains Mono at heavy weight, never below 11px, never below 4.5:1 contrast.
rules.board-is-the-roster: The lineup exists in exactly one place: the Konva pitch. Touch a token, pick a player in the modal; the bench is a chip list, not a second checklist.
rules.zero-data: With no records, bars stay at 0% and empty states say so in muted text. A bar that redistributes itself to fill the rail is a false reading.

narrative.overview:
Tracker Pro is not a stats app that happens to run during a match; it is an operations console that a coach reads at a glance from the bench of a stadium. The visual world is the pit wall at night: carbon-dark glass panels floating over a deep charcoal ground, hairline borders the way instrument housings have them, and one electric-blue accent that only ever lights up when something is live — the running clock, the active tab, the selected action, the open period. Everything else is a reading, not a decoration.

The system rejects the field-app green outright. Institutional green was the previous identity and it was cut entirely: there is no teal, no emerald, no purple, no indigo anywhere in the chrome. The only green left in the product is the literal green card of hockey (a physical object in the sport, therefore a literal object color, not a brand color). Because that exception exists, every other hue has to earn its place by meaning: blue is live and positive, red is negative, amber is discipline and attention, sky is transition and substitution, slate is neutral data.

Density is a feature and a constraint at once: the live view has to fit in 100vh with zero vertical scroll, on a tablet held in one hand under stadium light. That single rule drives most of the geometry — 44px minimum touch targets, 92px action tiles, a two-and-a-half second path from "event happened" to "event recorded". Numbers are always monospaced and always heavy, because a scoreboard is read at distance, not parsed.
keyCharacteristics: Carbon ground (slate-950) with translucent glass panels and slate-800 hairlines — depth from translucency, never from colored glow.
One accent color, electric blue, reserved for live state and primary actions.
Every figure in JetBrains Mono; every label in Outfit.
A single screen, no vertical scroll, in the live view.
Touch targets sized for fingers in motion: 44px floor, 92px for the action pad.
The lineup is drawn on the pitch, not checked off in a list.
Commit actions live in a full-width bottom bar, not inside a column.

rules.name: The Zero-Green Rule
rules.body: There is no green in the chrome — no teal, emerald, purple, or indigo anywhere in the shell, panels, tabs, buttons, chips, or charts. The only green permitted is the literal hockey green card. If a new surface wants color, it must come from the blue/red/amber/sky signal set.

rules.name: The Blue Means Live Rule
rules.body: Electric blue is a state, not a brand. It appears on the active tab, the active chip, the running clock context, the primary CTA, the Partido en Curso stage label, and the live badge — nowhere else. A screen that is blue everywhere is a screen where blue means nothing. Before a match starts, every live signal stays grey: the Partido tab is dimmed and dotted, the stage label reads Sin Iniciar, and the Estadísticas badge stays off.

rules.name: The Signal Color Rule
rules.body: A hue may only be used where it carries the event's polarity (positive / negative / discipline / transition / neutral). Decorative colorization of a control that carries no event meaning is out of bounds.

rules.name: The Mono Data Rule
rules.body: Every number the user reads as data — score, clock, KPI values, counters, minutes, zone values, ratio — is set in JetBrains Mono. Proportional digits in a live readout are a bug, not a style choice.

rules.name: The 11px Floor
rules.body: No data text may render below 11px. The 10px micro tier exists for uppercase non-numeric chrome only; the 9px tier that appears on the zone-selector caption is the single exception in the built app and must not be extended to any value-bearing surface.

rules.name: The 4.5:1 Rule
rules.body: No text ships below 4.5:1 contrast against its actual background. text-muted on the carbon ground is the darkest legal text; muted-on-muted is not.

rules.name: The Neutral Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted with the ground color, never with the accent. A blue shadow on a blue button is a glow; this system has no glows.

rules.name: The Two-Level Depth Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two surface levels: glass panel and inset. A third level of nesting means a new element is competing with the data.

rules.name: The Board Is The Roster Rule
rules.body: The lineup exists in exactly one place: the Konva pitch. Touch a token, pick a player in the modal; the bench is a chip list, not a second checklist. If a screen needs to show the eleven, it reads the board.

rules.name: The Zero-Data Rule
rules.body: With no records, bars stay at 0% and empty states say so in muted text. A bar that redistributes itself to fill the rail, or a KPI that renders as a placeholder, is a false reading — the absence of data must look like absence.

dos: Do reserve electric blue for live state and the primary commit action, so the color keeps meaning "now".
Do set every number in JetBrains Mono at heavy weight, and keep the score and clock as the two largest elements on screen.
Do keep the live view inside 100vh with no page-level vertical scroll — push overflow into the action pad, the player grid, or the feed, never the shell.
Do hold every touch target to at least 44px of height (56px+ when the layout allows) and keep action tiles at 92px.
Do express lineup and formation on the pitch, positioning tokens by touch and drag, with the bench as chips plus a modal — the board is the source of truth for alignment.
Do tint a control by the polarity of the data it carries (positive, negative, discipline, transition, neutral), using the signal palette — blue for positive, sky for substitution and transition.
Do keep the header at h-14 with the four tabs always visible, so navigation never costs a scroll or a back gesture.
Do keep text at or above 4.5:1 contrast and never let data fall below 11px.
Do put the commit CTA in the full-width bottom action bar (shrink-0 px-3 pb-3 → max-w-3xl mx-auto), so it is reachable from every column.
Do render a real tile for every action, even in a single-action category, and keep the tile keyboard-operable with role, tabindex, aria-label, Enter and Space.
Do keep the live signals honest: grey badge, Sin Iniciar, and a dimmed Partido tab until a match is actually running.
Do let empty states say so in muted text and leave ratio and distribution bars at 0% when there is nothing to show.
donts: Don't introduce green, teal, emerald, purple, or indigo into the chrome — the only green allowed is the literal green card.
Don't use colored shadows, glows, or neon bloom; every shadow is neutral.
Don't let the live view scroll vertically, and don't let any panel's content push the shell past 100vh.
Don't add colored gradients, illustrations, or decorative hues to the shell; the only gradient in the product is the primary button and the pitch canvas.
Don't set data in the proportional sans font, and don't animate the score with anything other than the sharp cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) scale.
Don't build alignment or formation as a list of checkboxes; it is set by placing tokens on the tactical board.
Don't shrink a control below the 44px floor or drop the label from an action tile to save space.
Don't reuse the semantic signal hues for generic decoration — a red chip that isn't a negative event is a bug.
Don't paint positive feed events sky, or paint the Pérdidas por Zona and Robos por Zona cards with different tones for the same metric.
Don't light the live badge, the stage label, or the Partido tab blue before a match is in progress.
